American College of Cardiology MAPLE-HCM trial summary, Principal Findings, Safety, Inclusion/Exclusion

studyDesign.population: Adults with symptomatic obstructive HCM; selected patients meeting functional and LV systolic function inclusion criteria

primaryEndpoint.name: Peak oxygen uptake change at week 24
primaryEndpoint.locator: NEJM original abstract Results, pVO2 week 24

safety.note: ACC secondary summary reports a death after brief viral illness; attribution cannot be independently assessed from this synopsis

evidenceLimitationsUnreviewed: The original peer-reviewed abstract gives no patient-level source data, CSR or full efficacy/safety tables.
The ACC detailed secondary effects and safety numbers are a cardiology-society summary, not independently authenticated original table extracts.
Limited 175-person sample and 24-week follow-up constrain assessment of uncommon, delayed and long-term safety risks.
Exclusions include atrial fibrillation or flutter and selected cardiovascular conditions, limiting generalizability.
Selected baseline ejection fraction and functional inclusion criteria limit extrapolation to other symptomatic HCM populations.
Observed change in left ventricular ejection fraction demands independent cardiac-function and dose-monitoring review.
Exercise capacity and symptom outcomes are not a direct demonstration of reduced mortality, hospitalization or lifelong durability.
Statistical plan, protocol amendments, endpoint hierarchy, multiplicity, database-lock and unblinding chronology remain independent-review questions.
Do not substitute results of SEQUOIA-HCM or other aficamten studies for exact MAPLE-HCM NCT05767346 results.
reviewQuestions: Verify original publisher full paper, underlying tables and authenticated registered protocol/SAP for NCT05767346.
Reconcile active metoprolol comparator, permitted dose titration, prior beta blocker withdrawal and patient baseline exclusion criteria.
Review CPET peak VO2 measurement validity, endpoint clinical importance and missingness for original 175 randomized participants.
Check secondary outcome multiplicity hierarchy and distinctions between physiological, quality-of-life and clinical-event endpoints.
Independently evaluate left ventricular ejection fraction reductions, any transient LVEF below safety limits, serious adverse events and reported death.
Determine applicability to patients with atrial fibrillation or reduced LVEF and whether additional long-term safety is expected at the study phase.
Assign qualified disease-specialist and independent biostatistician reviews after actual source authentication and owner approvals.
